translations.translation: B"S.
Motzaei Shabbos Parshas Lech Lecha – in his room – 5738

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two interpretations of "Lech Lecha," focusing on Avraham as the hidden intellect and the descent of his concealed light into Malchus.

translations.translation: "And Hashem said to Avram, 'Go for yourself from your land, from your birthplace, and from your father's house, to the land that I will show you.'"
And it is known
that there are two interpretations of this.
The first interpretation is that the going
(of "go for yourself")
is from above to below.
And as explained in Torah Ohr,
that Avram is "Av Ram" (Lofty Father),
the intellect that is hidden from all thought
[which is above even the level of Chochmah.
For Chochmah
(even though it is the beginning of all internal powers)
is a level of revelation.
In contrast, "Av Ram" is the intellect hidden from all thought.
And as explained in the glosses and explanations of the Tzemach Tzedek on Torah Ohr there,
[detailing the levels within this].
And Hashem said to Avram, "Go for yourself from your land," etc., that his concealed light should go out into revelation and be drawn from above to below until "to the land,"
the level of Malchus.
And it adds, "which I will show you,"
and regarding this there are two interpretations.
One
(according to its simple meaning)
is that "I will show you" refers to the land,
the level of Malchus,
for Malchus is the level of the revealed world, therefore it says about it "which I will show you."
And the second interpretation is that "I will show you" refers to Avram
(the level of the intellect hidden from all thought)
— "I will see and reveal you to yourself,"
("in your essence and your selfhood").
And this means,
that even though the Sefirah of Malchus, the revealed world
(and especially as it is drawn down into Biyah)
is the very lowest extremity,
and the intellect hidden from all thought
(which is hidden even from the highest thought)
is the very highest extremity,
nevertheless,
through the descent and drawing down
(of Avram,
the intellect hidden from all thought)
to "the land which I will show you"
(according to the first interpretation),
to the level of Malchus, the revealed world
(the lowest extremity),
through this the true nature
(his essence and selfhood)
of Avram will be seen and revealed
(according to the second interpretation),
such that an elevation occurs
(also)
in the level of the intellect hidden from all thought
(the very highest extremity),
as is understood from what is explained in Torah Ohr there.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section parallels the concept to the soul's descent into the body, explaining that through this descent an elevation occurs even in the highest level of Yechidah.

translations.translation: B)
And similarly, this applies to the matter of the soul's descent into the body,
that the elevation achieved in the soul through its descent below
[which is accomplished in the manner of a journey,
the concept of "go for yourself"],
is also in its most exalted levels,
and even in the level of Yechidah.
For even though it is called Yechidah because it "receives from the Singular One"
[and therefore
it is not possible for there to be something opposite it in the side of impurity,
"a reflection of a reflection they do not have"],
nevertheless,
through the soul descending below,
from a high roof to a deep pit,
an elevation is also effected in the level of Yechidah within it.
As explained in several discourses,
that specifically through the soul's service in its descent below, an elevation is effected
(an incomparable elevation)
also in the root and essence of the soul above.
And this is also understood from what is explained in several talks
(regarding the matter of an aliyah to the Torah),
that the elevation is in all five levels of the soul—Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah—
which are the three levels, lower, middle, and upper,
of the Teivas Noach.
And according to what was stated above
(based on the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov
on the verse
"Come... into the ark"),
that the concept of the Teivas Noach is "instruction in the order of service"
for every single Jew
[and especially after the month of Tishrei, when the order of service of "and Yaakov went on his way" begins.
For even though he goes on his way
(also)
in matters of the permitted and in mundane activities,
and even to the level of "mighty waters," which are all the troubles of livelihood, etc.,
nevertheless, by inserting himself into the "words" (teivos) of prayer and Torah, not only is he "saved from the floodwaters,"
but moreover, through the waters the ark is lifted up,
and even to the point that "the ark came to rest"],
it is understood from this,
that the elevation of the soul effected through its descent below and its enclothing in the "mighty waters" is in all three levels
(of the Teivas Noach)
—lower, middle, and upper—
which in the human soul correspond to Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah.
Analogous to what was explained above
(section 1),
that through the going and descent of Avram to the land, the level of Malchus,
the purpose
(of this descent)
being to bring about revelation in Biyah,
[and as is known,
that Avram's going to the land was in order to draw down into Biyah, even into this physical world,
through which he prepared the way for the drawing down through the performance of physical mitzvos after the giving of the Torah],
an elevation was also effected in the level of the intellect hidden from all thought.
